root_cause: Text.expand_tabs rebuilt the text by appending the padding spaces as a separate string styled with the Text's base style (self.style), so the padding lost any span styles that covered the tab. It also computed tab stops from character length (len) rather than cell width, so wide characters (emoji) produced the wrong number of spaces. In addition, Text.append / append_text / append_tokens created spans for empty-string styles ('' is not None), which left spurious Span(x, y, '') entries in the result.
best_solution: Add Span.extend(cells) (returns a Span with end+cells, or self if cells==0) and Text.extend_style(spaces) (no-op for spaces<=0; otherwise append spaces and extend every span whose end >= len(self), or just extend plain if no spans). Rewrite expand_tabs: for each line from split('\n', include_separator=True), pass lines without tabs through unchanged; otherwise split on '\t' with include_separator, replace the trailing tab of each part with one space, track cell_position += part.cell_len, and if cell_position % tab_size is nonzero call part.extend_style(tab_size - remainder); collect parts and Text('').join them, then copy plain/spans back into self. Change 'if style is not None' to 'if style' in append, append_text and append_tokens so empty styles add no spans. Also Text.tab_size default becomes None and __rich_console__ uses console.tab_size when self.tab_size is None. The reasoning: the style of the tab is exactly the set of spans ending at the tab's end, so extending those spans over the inserted spaces carries the style; tab stops are defined in terminal cells, not characters.
acceptable_alternatives: Any expand_tabs that (a) uses cell_len for tab stops, (b) extends every span covering the tab over the padding (producing exactly the per-part spans the tests list, e.g. Span(0,4,'bold'), Span(4,7,'bold') rather than one merged span), (c) emits no empty-style spans, and (d) exposes Text.extend_style(spaces) with the exact semantics above. The exact span list is asserted, so structurally different but visually equivalent span sets fail.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_text.py::test_tabs_to_spaces_spans (12 parametrized cases) asserts exact text._spans lists after expand_tabs, e.g. '[bold]foo\tbar' -> [Span(0,4,'bold'), Span(4,7,'bold')], '\tbar' -> [] (no empty-style spans), '[bold]💩💩💩💩\t💩' tab_size 8 -> '💩💩💩💩        💩' (cell-width tab stops) with [Span(0,12,'bold'), Span(12,13,'bold')]. tests/test_text.py::test_extend_style requires a new public method Text.extend_style(spaces): 0 and -1 are no-ops; extend_style(2) on '[red]foo[/red] [bold]bar' gives 'foo bar  ' with spans [Span(0,3,'red'), Span(4,9,'bold')]. test_tabs_to_spaces also checks Text('No Tabs', style='bold') keeps style. tests/test_panel.py::test_render_size expects the title rule to be one merged Segment, which only happens once empty-style spans are no longer appended (the 'if style:' change).
locating_signals: Statement names Text.extend_tabs (actually expand_tabs, a typo) and says padding spaces should inherit the tab's style(s), which points at rich/text.py expand_tabs. It does not mention cell width, empty-style spans, the Text.extend_style or Span.extend helpers, or the Panel rendering change; those come only from the hidden tests.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed in the Kaggle env. Every agent made a one-line style change in the old expand_tabs loop: v4 and v8 swapped _style for part.style (the Text's base style, which for markup text is '' and so still unstyled), v6 searched part._spans for a span covering the tab char, v7 took the span ending at len(part). None switched to cell_len, so emoji cases produced 4 spaces instead of 8; none removed the empty-style spans (the log shows Span(0,5,''), Span(5,8,'') noise), so even simple cases like '\tbar' failed their exact-span assertion; none added Text.extend_style (AttributeError); and test_panel::test_render_size still failed. v6/v7/v8 also added their own test files. The v4 run: 12 failed, 100 passed.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement is a short PR description and the fix touches a data structure with a precise internal representation (spans, offsets, segments), expect the hidden tests to assert that exact representation, not just the visible output. Reproduce the bug with a few inputs, then print the internal structure (e.g. _spans) for plain, styled, multi-line and wide-character (emoji/CJK) inputs and make each one minimal and clean: no empty or duplicate entries, and widths in display cells rather than len(). Also prefer adding a small reusable public helper named after the operation the statement describes ('extend style') over an inline hack, because upstream authors usually add one and test it directly.
